Offsets_only index: existence iff offsets[pid+1] > offsets[pid]

filters.predicate: production_year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2008 AND title LIKE '%Kung%Fu%Panda%'
note LIKE '%(200%)%' AND (note LIKE '%(USA)%' OR note LIKE '%(worldwide)%')
info_type_id = it_rd AND (info LIKE 'Japan:%2007%' OR info LIKE 'USA:%2008%')
note = '(voice)' AND role_id = rt_actress AND person_role_id IS NOT NULL

data_structures.dim_ids: scalar constants (rt_actress, it_rd, cc_us, g_f) resolved via single scan
data_structures.title_driver: small flat_array<uint32_t> of surviving title ids + parallel array of title strings for MIN
data_structures.mc_filter: per-movie inline scan via offsets_only index, no materialization
data_structures.mi_filter: per-movie inline scan via offsets_only index
data_structures.ci_filter: per-movie inline scan via offsets_only index

data_structures.aggregation: two scalar string accumulators for MIN(n.name) and MIN(t.title)

parallelism.notes: Parallelize title scan over morsels (2.5M rows). After title filter survivors are tiny — process serially or with per-thread MIN accumulators reduced at end.

implementation_notes: Step 1: single-pass resolve constants rt_actress (role_type.role='actress'), it_rd (info_type.info='release dates'), cc_us (company_name.country_code='[us]' as a precomputed bitset/set since 234,997 rows), g_f (name.gender byte == 'f').
Actually cc_us has 234k+ rows — DO NOT enumerate; instead, per mc row look up company_name.country_code[mc.company_id] and compare to '[us]' (or compute the byte-equality once).

Step 2: parallel scan title.production_year for [2007,2008]; for surviving rows fetch t.title via offsets+dat; apply three-substring scan ('Kung','Fu','Panda' in order). Collect surviving t.id list (expected <=5 rows).

Step 3: for each surviving t.id, iterate mc via movie_companies__movie_id offsets. For each mc row: check note has '(200' followed by ')' and contains either '(USA)' or '(worldwide)'; then check company_name.country_code[mc.company_id]=='[us]'. Bail at first satisfying mc row (only existence needed).

Step 4: similarly verify mi existence: iterate mi rows for t.id, require info_type_id==it_rd, info not null, and (prefix 'Japan:' AND contains '2007') OR (prefix 'USA:' AND contains '2008'). Existence sufficient.

Step 5: iterate ci rows for t.id; for each row require note length==7 and memcmp '(voice)', role_id==rt_actress, person_role_id != NULL. Read pid=person_id; check name.gender[pid]=='f', fetch n.name and require contains 'Angel'. Check aka_name existence via offsets_only index for pid.
Step 6: if all conditions hold for this ci row → candidate. Update MIN(n.name) with name string, MIN(t.title) with title string.
Per-thread MINs reduced at end via lexicographic comparison.
